summary: Modoc National Forest lookout first staffed 1911 by Eli Dale; destroyed by fire in 2000 and rebuilt as an accessible station with a chairlift in 2001.

facts.design: 2001 structure: accessible station with extra-wide catwalk and a power chairlift from ground level to the catwalk
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Modoc National Forest

staffing.status: permanently manned lookout on the Forest (1920 newsletter)

events.note: Register: primary lookout established at this point in 1911; 1950 and 2001 structures followed
Eli Dale, first lookout man; a 1920 California District News Letter item (Aug 28, 1920) says he assumed duty in 1912
1919 item: Dale employed as lookout for the past seven years
Fire caused by an electrical problem while the lookout was away for the night
New accessible structure with extra-wide catwalk and power chairlift

corrections.why: The register text cuts the forest name off at 'Fores'; the same page gives Modoc National Forest as the location.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and the weebly history give 1911 for the primary lookout with Dale as first lookout man. A 1920 California District News Letter item (August 28, 1920), quoted on the weebly page, says Dale assumed duty in 1912. Story gives 1911 as the establishment date and notes the 1912 account.
The brief lists two coordinate pairs. The register's 41.415829, -121.109211 is used; the other pair was not checked against a source read, so it is not used.

notes_for_editor: Brief events omitted the 1950 replacement, 2000 fire and 2001 rebuild; added from the register. No source read gives current visiting arrangements, so access is omitted. Two Modoc Forest PDFs surfaced by search returned 404 and were not used. A WebSearch hit describing a 2000 fire and 2001 rebuild with a lift referred to a Montana site (Sula Peak), and was not used. Dale history comes from newspaper and district newsletter items quoted on the weebly page; the originals were not checked.
